rounds.text: Alufluoride Ltd trades at a modest P/E of 17.3x while showing extraordinary fundamental momentum, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 116% over the last five years and 71% over the trailing twelve months [E1, E17, E19]. Valuation models indicate significant disconnect from reality, as a discounted cash flow intrinsic value sits at Rs 1669 per share against the market price of Rs 709, leaving a substantial 57.5% margin of safety [E42, E43]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's price requires only 6.2% earnings growth, whereas the base case assumes 18.0%, proving that expectations are severely anchored below operational delivery [E44]. Profitability metrics remain exceptionally robust, with a 5-year median ROE of 19%, a current ROE of 22.0%, and a ROCE of 24.2% [E12, E13, E24]. Operating margins are expanding rapidly, jumping from 20% to 26% over three years and reaching 36% in September 2026, while strong cash conversion of 1.88x ensures profits are fully backed by ₹ 47 Cr in operating cash flow [E27, E28, E31, E32]. Conceded: [E6] P/E of 17.23x against a sector benchmark of 5.97x, [E11] EV/EBITDA of 10.49x against a sector benchmark of 5.91x, and [E36] borrowings rising to Rs 54 Cr in Sep 2026.

While the headline valuation multiples may look moderate at a P/E of 17.3x [E1], the company trades at a notable premium when evaluated against sector benchmarks, with a P/E of 17.23x compared to the sector benchmark of just 5.97x [E6]. This elevated pricing is further underscored by a P/B of 3.92x against a sector benchmark of 2.68x and an EV/EBITDA of 10.49x compared to its sector benchmark of 5.91x [E7, E11]. Furthermore, profitability and efficiency metrics trail behind the broader sector, as demonstrated by an ROA of 14.69% against a sector benchmark of 29.16%, and an ROCE of 23.31% lagging the sector benchmark of 41.71% [E8, E10]. Top-line momentum has also stalled in the immediate term, with compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months flatlining at 0% [E16]. Balance sheet pressures are evident as borrowings increased to Rs 54 Cr in September 2026, up from Rs 45 Cr a year prior [E36], alongside domestic institutional holdings dropping from 1.28% to 0.47% [E40]. Moreover, operating and quarterly margin trends are explicitly characterized as inconsistent over recent periods [E29, E30]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong 5-year profit growth of 116% [E17] alongside solid cash conversion and operating cash flows [E31, E32].

Conceded: the bear correctly notes the premium to sector P/E, P/B, and EV/EBITDA benchmarks, as well as the 0% TTM sales growth [E6, E7, E11, E16]. However, sector comparisons ignore the company's superior fundamental momentum, evidenced by a stellar 22.76% ROE that vastly outperforms the 1.78% sector benchmark [E9]. The bear's concern over rising borrowings to Rs 54 Cr [E36] is countered by a dramatic -91.3% drop in CWIP, signaling that major capital expenditure has wrapped up and new income-generating capacity is coming online [E37]. Furthermore, the bear's fixation on inconsistent margin trends [E29, E30] overlooks explosive recent expansion, including a quarterly operating margin hitting 36% in September 2026—an 11 percentage point year-over-year jump [E28]. While domestic institutions trimmed holdings [E40], overall institutional money flow registers as positive with a holding change of +0.47 percentage points [E41]. Finally, the backward-looking critique on margins misses the powerful reality of stellar cash conversion at 1.88x, ensuring that a massive 71% TTM profit growth is fully backed by real cash [E19, E31].

Conceded: ROE vastly outperforms the sector benchmark [E9], and quarterly operating margin reached 36% in September 2026 [E28]. However, the bull's dismissal of sector valuation premiums [E6, E7, E11] ignores that the company's valuation multiples—including a P/E of 17.23x against a sector benchmark of 5.97x—are severely stretched compared to peers [E6]. Furthermore, pointing to positive institutional money flow [E41] glosses over the concrete reality that domestic institutions have actively trimmed their holdings from 1.28% to 0.47% [E40]. While the bull celebrates the completion of capital expenditure via plunging CWIP [E37], borrowings simultaneously climbed to Rs 54 Cr from Rs 45 Cr a year prior [E36], introducing rising financial risk. Finally, the heavy reliance on explosive short-term metrics bypasses the persistent structural vulnerability of inconsistent yearly and quarterly margin trends [E29, E30] and stagnant 0% trailing twelve-month sales growth [E16].
